items.summary:
CRO review: retain containment this cycle. Delivery is saturated at 10/10 slots, so create no new proposals, change requests, research requests, telemetry, spend, deployments, credentials, or domain work. After the existing saveusfarms.com repair-or-close case releases one slot, execute only the canonical allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement against the recorded 61-click baseline; measure registered affiliate clicks for 14 days or 100 relevant impressions/clicks, with deterministic accessibility, disclosure, link, build, smoke, and rollback checks. Revenue and causal lift remain unknown.

Deferred revenue experiments: (1) allthingsmasonic.com CTA hierarchy and disclosure-preserving merchandising refinement; (2) one-at-a-time SEO tests for marineactivity.com AIS codes, greatamericanlakes.com Erie muskie, or xxxtea.com gallery, using existing GSC baselines, indexability/canonical/link validation, a 14-day or 100-relevant-impression window, and single-diff rollback; (3) affiliate attribution hygiene requiring registered tracking IDs before any ROI claim. Do not duplicate existing routed work.

Deferred product opportunities: MarkItDown (MIT; lab evidence supported) could normalize approved source documents into Markdown for a disposable content-discovery prototype. Expected metric: editor processing time or validated internal-link/content-brief quality; time-to-learn: one isolated prototype; smallest reversible prototype: convert a fixed, non-production fixture set and compare output manually. Risks: dependency and parser maintenance, malformed or adversarial documents, provenance/copyright handling, and no demonstrated conversion impact. shadcn/ui (MIT; bounded checks passed) could provide accessible reusable CTA/card primitives. Expected metric: component test coverage, accessibility defects, and implementation cycle time; time-to-learn: one preview-only component; smallest prototype: reproduce the allthingsmasonic CTA surface without adding dependencies to production. Risks: framework/build compatibility, dependency supply chain, styling drift, and no proven revenue lift. Mermaid (MIT; lab fit supported, no native checks) could generate editorial diagrams for selected guides. Expected metric: qualified organic clicks or engaged sessions on one instrumented page; time-to-learn: one static preview; smallest prototype: render one hand-authored diagram from a fixed fixture with no runtime generation. Risks: client-side payload/performance, untrusted diagram input, accessibility quality, maintenance, and unclear SEO lift. These remain research specifications only until capacity, CTO/security review, and measurement readiness are available.
